title: Immediate response to financial cyber fraud
guidance: Report financial cyber fraud immediately by calling 1930.
Use the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal at https://www.cybercrime.gov.in/.
Keep the transaction ID, transaction date, amount, bank or wallet details, and available transaction screenshots ready.
Contact your bank or payment provider through its official channel.

title: Preserve cybercrime evidence
guidance: Keep original messages, emails, transaction receipts, screenshots, relevant URLs, and chat transcripts.
Record the incident date and time when known.
Keep original files unchanged and work with copies when preparing a summary.
Review extracted information against the original evidence before using it in a complaint.
source_name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal FAQ

title: Report other cybercrime
guidance: Use the official National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal to find the appropriate reporting category.
Provide accurate incident details and relevant supporting evidence.
Review all details before submitting a complaint through the official portal.
source_name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal FAQ

title: Guidance for phishing and suspicious emails
guidance: Do not click suspicious links or open unexpected attachments.
Preserve the original email, including the sender address, subject, date, time, and full email headers when available.
Record suspicious URLs without opening them.
If you entered a password on a suspicious website, change it using the official website and enable multi-factor authentication where available.
If you shared banking information or lost money, contact your bank immediately and report financial cyber fraud by calling 1930 in India.
Report the incident through the official National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and review all details before submission.
source_name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal FAQ
